name: Orgrimmar
summary: Orgrimmar rises from the red canyons of northern Durotar as the orcs’ fortified capital and the New Horde’s heart. Trolls, tauren, and Forsaken allies also find shelter within its walls.

sections.title: A Home Chiseled from Stone
sections.body: Orgrimmar grew from the orcs’ search for a homeland after the Third War. Warchief Thrall led them to Kalimdor’s arid coasts, seeking freedom from demonic corruption and human bondage. He named the harsh land Durotar for his father and the city for his fallen mentor, Orgrim Doomhammer. Building the stronghold cost blood and sweat. With help from the tauren, Darkspear trolls, goblin engineers, and the Champion Rexxar, the Horde drove back centaur, harpies, and ferocious thunder lizards that threatened the canyons.

sections.title: Valleys of the Horde
sections.body: Rugged mountains shield Orgrimmar from foreign invaders and Durotar’s violent razor-winds. The city’s natural hollows give each valley its own place in Horde life. The Valley of Strength holds the civic gatehouse, with a route deeper into the trade bazaar of The Drag. Tauren druids and shaman gather by the pools in the Valley of Wisdom. Darkspear shadow hunters and witch doctors live among the stilted pavilions of the Valley of Spirits.

sections.title: Shadows in the Red Rock
sections.body: Below the Valley of Honor and the heights of Grommash Hold, another life stirs beneath Orgrimmar. Warlocks and rogues practice in the cavern called the Cleft of Shadow, where Thrall keeps a close watch and grudgingly allows their arts. Farther below, Ragefire Chasm winds through volcanic tunnels beneath the canyon floor. Dark cultists and subterranean beasts fester there, threatening the fortress from within its own foundations.

aliases: who is in charge of orgrimmar
faq.answer: Warchief Thrall rules Orgrimmar from Grommash Hold. He leads the New Horde with honor, survival, and shamanistic heritage in mind, alongside Darkspear chieftain Vol'jin and veteran commander Varok Saurfang.

faq.q: Why is the city named Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: Thrall named Orgrimmar for Orgrim Doomhammer, the legendary former Warchief. Orgrim broke the shadow council's hold on the Old Horde and, before dying in battle, passed his warplate and the Doomhammer to Thrall.

faq.q: Who lives in Orgrimmar besides orcs?
faq.answer: Orgrimmar is home to the Darkspear troll tribe, whose members live in the Valley of Spirits, and welcomes visiting tauren ambassadors in the Valley of Wisdom. A contingent of Forsaken emissaries also has a presence in the city after their recent entry into the Horde.

faq.q: What is the Cleft of Shadow?
faq.answer: The Cleft of Shadow is a dim cavernous fissure beneath the canyon bluffs, off The Drag. The city's rogue and warlock guilds make their home there, keeping illicit trade and dangerous demonic invocations secluded from civilian districts.

faq.q: What threats exist inside the city?
faq.answer: Ragefire Chasm lies directly below the Cleft of Shadow. Its volcanic fissures teem with troggs, searing elementals, and treacherous warlocks who seek to undermine Thrall's rule from the depths.

faq.q: How do you travel to other continents from Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: Goblin-engineered zeppelins dock atop towers outside Orgrimmar’s main gate. They make regular flights across the Great Sea to Tirisfal Glades near Undercity and south to Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale.

angles.text: As a champion of the Horde, you find weaponmasters, class mentors, and trade hubs in its military and cultural seat. Warchief Thrall also receives audiences here.
As an orc, you can see Orgrimmar as hard-won freedom from demonic lethargy and internment, and as your people’s proud ancestral fortress on Durotar’s soil.
As a Darkspear troll, you have found lasting sanctuary alongside the orcs after losing the Darkspear Isles. The Valley of Spirits is your secure spiritual home.
As a shaman, you follow Thrall’s restoration of shamanism to the heart of Horde leadership. In the tranquil Valley of Wisdom, practitioners study the elements and commune with ancestral spirits.
As a warlock, you find an uneasy refuge in the Cleft of Shadow. Thrall keeps watch as you hone your dark arts, secluded from open judgment.
